thread:
jess: Quick question — onboarding a service account for the new logs-pipeline. We want least-privilege. Does it need org-level roles or can we keep everything project-scoped?

matt: keep it project-scoped if possible. org-level grants are harder to audit and increase blast radius. What does the pipeline need to do? write logs? write to GCS/S3?

jess: it needs to ingest app logs and ship them to a central bucket + write structured Log entries to the logging system. No access to other projects.

sarah: for that, two scoped bindings usually work: 1) project-level role for logging ingestion (e.g., roles/logging.logWriter on the project) 2) bucket-specific IAM for the central storage (grant the SA objectCreator on the target bucket). Avoid Owner/editor at org or project.

alice: agree. Also ensure the SA has no iam.serviceAccountUser on broad folders/orgs. If you need to impersonate, use short-lived tokens via a dedicated impersonation service account.

jess: sweet. any redaction/privacy notes? logs might include user emails/IDs for debugging in some messages.

sarah: yes — redact PII before shipping. We have a lightweight sidecar sanitizer for stackdriver/Fluentd that strips emails and hashes IDs. If you can't sanitize upstream, mark logs as sensitive and restrict access to the central bucket IAM to a smaller group + require double-approval for granting READ.

matt: practical IAM bindings I'd do:
```
- projects/my-project/serviceAccounts/logs-pipeline-sa@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com:
  - roles/logging.logWriter (project)
  - roles/storage.objectCreator (on projects/_/buckets/redwood-central-logs)
```
Also add an audit log exclusion? avoid excluding logging relevant to security — only exclude debug noise.

jess: thanks, that's clear. Who should approve the bucket grant?

sarah: security + infra leads. Please open an access request in the infra-requests channel with the svc account email and justification. Add a short ACL review checklist: retention, encryption (CMEK/KMS), and data residency.

jess: will do. One last: do we need to add any console roles for engineers to view logs? or should they go through the Console RBAC role split?

alice: use the console scoped read-only role (projects/my-project/roles/consoleLogViewer) — we have that custom role for safe log viewing without admin perms. Add users to a group rather than individually.

jess: perfect. I'll open the infra request and tag @sarah + @matt. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
